audit_notes: All parameters positive and inside bounds. Flexural rigidity D = E t^3/(12(1-nu^2)) = 5e5*8e-12/(12*0.7599) = 4.39e-7 N m. The formulation integrates the known bending-moment distribution of a clamped-clamped strip under uniform pressure, M(xi) = (p a^2/12)(6 xi - 6 xi^2 - 1), so d2w/dxi2 = (p a^4/D)(1 - 6 xi + 6 xi^2)/12 with w(0) = w(1) = 0 reproduces the clamped solution exactly (zero end slopes follow from symmetry and zero mean moment). Result: w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 1.90e-4 m (0.95 t). Peak surface strain at the clamped edges: eps = (t/2)*kappa_edge = (t/2)*p a^2/(12 D) = 16 t w_max / a^2 = 0.152, above the assumed critical detachment strain of 0.10 for biofilm; at mid-span eps = 0.076. Caveats: (1) w_max ~ t, so membrane stretching (von Karman) stiffens the skin and lowers the real strain by an estimated 15-30 %; the margin above 0.10 remains small, and 3 kPa would restore it. (2) Hydrostatic load: at 10 m draft the ambient pressure is ~100 kPa; the channels must be pressure-compensated (ambient + actuation pressure), otherwise the 200 um skin over a 2 mm span collapses onto the channel floor or bursts. (3) Fatigue: a few cycles per day over 5 years is ~1e4 cycles at 15 % strain, well inside PDMS fatigue life, but the skin-to-rib bond line is the stress concentration and must be designed (fillet, primer). (4) Only biofilm and early settlers are removed; adult barnacles with calcareous bases (critical removal stress ~0.1-1 MPa) are not. (5) The drag benefit is indirect: slime films add ~10-20 % skin friction; the solved field (deflection/strain) cannot compute this, and there is no conventional design with non-zero strain to compare with (a static fouling-release coating has zero actuation strain, which would make a relative gain undefined). Therefore no baseline_parameters are given; the gain is reported as not available and the drag benefit is documented here.
